summary: Describes an optional extension to IS-IS that adds checksums to CSNP and PSNP packets. The original protocol relied on lower layers to detect corruption, but experience showed this does not always hold. IS-IS is a link-state interior routing protocol used by ISPs.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo adds an optional Fletcher checksum to selected IS-IS messages. Routers that support it can detect corruption while still accepting messages from implementations that omit the checksum.

questions: what is the is-is optional checksum
what is the optional is-is checksum tlv
which is-is pdus can carry a checksum
how does rfc 3358 handle packets without checksums
subtitle: An optional checksum TLV for selected IS-IS protocol data units.

tldr.problem: IS-IS CSNP, PSNP, and IIH packets may be corrupted when lower layers or link hardware do not detect errors.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an optional TLV carrying a Fletcher checksum over the complete PDU. A supporting receiver discards a PDU with an incorrect checksum.
tldr.outcome: Implementations must still accept PDUs without the optional checksum, allowing the extension to coexist with implementations that do not support it.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 3358 as Informational and records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. The memo describes an optional extension to IS-IS.

sections.title: Why Add a Checksum
sections.content:
IS-IS originally relied on underlying layers to verify information in Complete Sequence Number PDUs (CSNPs), Partial Sequence Number PDUs (PSNPs), and IS-IS Hello PDUs (IIHs). The memo says faulty layer-2 implementations or network technologies without checksums can allow corruption through.

Corrupted length or TLV-length fields could cause a receiving node to generate many empty Link State PDUs. RFC 3358 therefore proposes an optional checksum TLV for these message types.
sections.plainLanguage: IS-IS expected the underlying network to catch damaged data. The memo adds an optional check for cases where that assumption fails.

sections.title: The Optional Checksum TLV
sections.content:
The TLV may appear in CSNP, PSNP, and IIH packets. It has type 12, length 2, and a 16-bit checksum. The checksum is a Fletcher checksum computed over the complete PDU after adding the TLV with an initial checksum value of zero.

An implementation that supports the extension MUST accept PDUs without the TLV. If it receives a checksum TLV and supports it, it MUST discard the PDU when the checksum is incorrect. It must discard the PDU if more than one checksum TLV appears or if the TLV appears in another PDU type.
sections.plainLanguage: The checksum TLV carries a value calculated over the whole PDU. A supporting router checks it and discards a damaged packet.

sections.title: Interaction with Signatures
sections.content:
An implementation supporting optional checksums MUST accept a PDU whose checksum value is zero and consider that checksum correct. An implementation that does not support the extension must accept a PDU containing the checksum TLV.

If a PDU contains signatures such as HMAC or MD5 that provide equivalent or stronger functionality, an implementation must omit the optional checksum on that interface or send a zero value. This avoids changing the data used to compute the signature.
sections.plainLanguage: Older implementations can ignore the optional checksum. When a signature covers the packet, the checksum is omitted or set to zero so it does not interfere with signature calculation.
